titles.581: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR — Pelagian telum: sin-in-Adam = hereditary corruption?
titles.582: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR — when corrupted in Adam? same reductio as before
titles.583: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Apostle never said we sinned in Adam; sense = derived corruption
titles.584: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Adam corrupted when he first sinned; we when born
titles.585: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — corruptus in Adamo ≠ corruptus simpliciter; root before branches
titles.586: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC tip — fights pre-existence imputation; tip before GAR 4 (act+corruption)

latin.581: GAR. 3. Sed & Pelagianus telum arripiet, & in nos contorquebit. Nam ubi dicit Apostolus nos in Adamo peccasse, quid intelligit Vir doctus peccati voce? Corruptionem haereditariam, vitium illud originale nostrum, & nobis ingenitum. Itaque in Adamo peccasse, erit in Adamo corruptos & vitiatos esse.
latin.582: Insurget iam Pelagianus, & hac argumentatione fretus quaeret, Quando corrupti sumus in Adamo peccato eius? An cum ipse peccavit, & peccando se corrupit, an alio tempore? Certe cum ipse peccavit, & peccando se corrupit. Multi, imo omnes peccato pro nobis, sed & vitio illius lapsi moniti sunt. Audi iam. Qui ita corrupti fuerunt, ut mortis aeternae rei facti sint, illi vere & proprie corrupti fuerunt. Qui vere & proprie corrupti fuerunt, illi tunc cum corrupti sunt, vere & proprie fuerunt. Ergone infans qui nunc nascitur, vere fuit, cum Adamus peccaret, & peccando seipsum corrumperet? Ita qui laqueos aliis confecerant, in eos se induunt, & quam foveam aliis paraverant in eam ipsimet incidunt.
latin.583: PLAC. Hi laquei nulli sunt, neque facile expedio. Primum enim Apostolus non dixit nos in Adamo peccasse, & ut dixisset, propositio nos esse corruptos & vitiatos in Adamo quem sensum habere possit, considerandum est. Sensus est nos derivata ab Adamo corruptione corruptos esse, vel, quod eodem redit, corruptionem Adami fuisse fontem unde nostra scaturiit corruptio, vel, corruptum fuisse Adamum, & corruptionem Adami in nos propagatam fuisse.
latin.584: Si ergo quaero, Quando Adamus corruptus fuit? respondebo, cum primum peccavit. Quando corrupti fuimus vi communionis quam cum Adamo habemus? Resp. quando geniti sumus. Quid est in ea re difficultatis?
latin.585: Taceo Virum doctum uti fallacia a dicto secundum quid ad dictum simpliciter. Aliud enim est esse corruptum secundum quid, seu cum hac limitatione in Adamo, aliud esse corruptum simpliciter seu absque eiusmodi limitatione. Hoc ex illo non sequitur, si temporis illius ratio habeatur, cum primum Adamus corruptus fuit: significatur enim corruptio radicis seu fontis, non ramorum aut rivorum, quoniam nondum erant: prius autem est esse quam esse corruptum.
latin.586: Id quod mihi respondere non potest, quoniam, ut iam observavi, imputationem oppugno quae diu fuisse creditur, antequam esse inciperemus, & qua factum sit ut vere & proprie peccatores & rei fieremus.

pass_a.581: GAR arms a Pelagian dart: if 'sin in Adam' means only our inborn hereditary vice, then to sin in Adam is merely to be corrupt and spoiled in him. Keep the pressure.
pass_a.582: Then the Pelagian rises with the same timing trap: when were we corrupted in Adam by his sin—only when he sinned and corrupted himself? Whoever was so corrupted as to be guilty of eternal death then was truly and properly corrupted, and so then truly was. Therefore today's newborn already was when Adam fell. Those who set snares for others put themselves into them, and fall into the pit they dug.
pass_a.583: Placeus: no real snare. Paul never said we sinned in Adam. Even the phrase 'corrupt in Adam' means corruption derived from him as fountain, or his corruption propagated into us—not a proper co-timing of our being with his first fall.
pass_a.584: Ask the times apart. When was Adam corrupted? When he first sinned. When were we corrupted by the communion we have with him? When we were begotten. What difficulty remains in that split?
pass_a.585: I set aside his slide from a saying in a certain respect to a saying simply. To be corrupt 'in Adam' with that limit is not the same as to be corrupt without limit. From the former, at the hour when Adam was first corrupted, you get only the root's corruption—not the branches or streams, which were not yet. Being is prior to being corrupt.
pass_a.586: He cannot answer that root-and-branch point, because—as already noted—I am opposing an imputation believed to have stood long before we began to be, and by which we supposedly became true sinners and guilty. Tip before GAR 4 joins Adam's act with the corruption it begot.

581: GAR. 3. But the Pelagian also will seize a dart, and will twist it against us. For where the Apostle says that we have sinned in Adam, what does the learned man understand by the word sin? Hereditary corruption, that original vice of ours, and inborn in us. And so to have sinned in Adam will be to have been corrupt and vitiated in Adam.
582: The Pelagian will now rise, and relying on this argumentation will ask, When were we corrupted in Adam by his sin? When he himself sinned, and by sinning corrupted himself, or at another time? Surely when he himself sinned, and by sinning corrupted himself. Many, nay all, have been warned by the sin for us, but also by the vice of that fall. Hear now. Those who were so corrupted that they were made guilty of eternal death, those were truly and properly corrupted. Those who were truly and properly corrupted, those then when they were corrupted truly and properly were. Therefore has the infant who is now born truly been, when Adam was sinning, and by sinning corrupting himself? So those who had made snares for others put themselves into them, and into the pit which they had prepared for others they themselves fall.
583: PLAC. These snares are none, nor do I easily get free. For first the Apostle has not said that we have sinned in Adam, and even if he had said it, what sense the proposition that we are corrupt and vitiated in Adam can have must be considered. The sense is that we are corrupted by corruption derived from Adam, or, which comes to the same, that Adam's corruption was the fountain from which our corruption sprang, or, that Adam was corrupted, and Adam's corruption was propagated into us.
584: If therefore I ask, When was Adam corrupted? I will answer, when he first sinned. When were we corrupted by force of the communion which we have with Adam? Answer, when we were begotten. What difficulty is there in that matter?
585: I pass over that the learned man uses the fallacy from what is said in a certain respect to what is said simply. For it is one thing to be corrupt in a certain respect, or with this limitation in Adam, another to be corrupt simply or without such a limitation. This does not follow from that, if the reason of that time is had, when Adam was first corrupted: for the corruption of the root or fountain is signified, not of the branches or streams, because they were not yet. But it is prior to be than to be corrupt.
586: Which he cannot answer me, because, as I have already observed, I oppose the imputation which is believed to have long been, before we began to be. And by that imputation it was brought about that we truly and properly became sinners and guilty.

581.choice: Pelagian: sin-in-Adam read as inborn corruption only

582.choice: When corrupted? → infant already was when Adam fell

583.choice: No 'sinned in Adam' text; means derived/propagated corruption

584.choice: Adam at first sin; we at birth by communion

585.choice: secundum quid ≠ simpliciter; root before branches

586.choice: Targets pre-existence imputation; tip before GAR 4
